pattern_note: This is the INC model blueprint as adopted by most health-science universities. Universities may add choice (for example 'answer any one of two essays') or split essays into sub-parts (2 + 4 + 4, 2 + 5 + 8 and so on). This question bank covers the descriptive part only (2, 5, 10 and 15 marks); the 1-mark MCQ block is left out on purpose.

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Cardiovascular Disorders (including BCLS)
units.topics: Hypertension; arteriosclerosis and peripheral vascular disease; coronary artery disease, angina and myocardial infarction; valvular and rheumatic heart disease; infective endocarditis; dysrhythmias and heart block; heart failure; cardiogenic shock and cardiac tamponade; cardiopulmonary arrest; basic cardiac life support (BCLS) module

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Haematological Disorders
units.topics: Anaemias; polycythaemia; bleeding disorders - haemophilia, ITP, DIC; thalassaemia; leukaemia, leukopenia and agranulocytosis; lymphomas and multiple myeloma

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Integumentary Disorders

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Musculoskeletal Disorders
units.topics: Dislocation, fracture, sprain, strain, contusion, amputation; osteomyelitis and bone tumours; casts, splints, traction and crutch walking; bursitis, synovitis and arthritis; osteoporosis, osteomalacia and Paget's disease; spinal deformities and disc prolapse; rehabilitation, prostheses and joint replacement

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Communicable Diseases
units.topics: Overview of the infectious process; tuberculosis; diarrhoeal diseases; viral hepatitis A to E; typhoid; herpes, chickenpox, measles, mumps, influenza; meningitis; gas gangrene; leprosy; dengue, malaria, chikungunya, plague, filariasis, swine flu; diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, poliomyelitis; COVID-19; isolation, quarantine and immunisation

units.title: Drugs used on Urinary System
units.topics: Pharmacology of commonly used drugs: renin–angiotensin system; diuretics and antidiuretics; drugs toxic to the kidney; urinary antiseptics; treatment of UTI – acidifiers and alkalinisers

units.title: Drugs acting on Nervous System
units.topics: Analgesics – NSAIDs, antipyretics, opioids and other central analgesics; general anaesthesia (techniques, pre-anaesthetic medication) and local anaesthetics; medical gases (oxygen, nitrous oxide, carbon dioxide); hypnotics and sedatives; skeletal muscle relaxants; antipsychotics and mood stabilisers; antidepressants; antianxiety drugs; anticonvulsants; drugs for neurodegenerative disorders; CNS stimulants; ethyl alcohol and treatment of methyl alcohol poisoning

units.title: Drugs used for Hormonal Disorders and Supplementation, Contraception and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
units.topics: Oestrogens and progestins; oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy; vaginal contraceptives; drugs for infertility and medical termination of pregnancy; uterine stimulants and relaxants (tocolytics)

units.title: Drugs used for Pregnant Women during Antenatal Period, Labour and Postnatal Period
units.topics: Tetanus prophylaxis; iron and vitamin K1 supplementation; oxytocin and misoprostol; ergometrine; methyl prostaglandin F2-alpha; magnesium sulphate; calcium gluconate

units.title: Miscellaneous Drugs
units.topics: Drugs used for de-addiction; drugs used in CPR and emergency (adrenaline, chlorpheniramine, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone); IV fluids and electrolyte replacement; common poisons, drugs used for treatment of poisoning (activated charcoal, ipecac, antidotes, anti-snake venom); vitamins and minerals supplementation; vaccines and sera (Universal Immunization Programme schedule); anticancer drugs – chemotherapeutic drugs commonly used; immunosuppressants and immunostimulants

units.title: Introduction to Drugs used in Alternative Systems of Medicine
units.topics: Ayurveda, Homeopathy, Unani and Siddha – principles and drugs used for common ailments; AYUSH; safety, interactions and the nurse's role

units.topics: Kidney and urinary tract – glomerulonephritis, pyelonephritis, renal calculi, cystitis, renal cell carcinoma, renal failure (acute and chronic); male genital system – cryptorchidism, testicular atrophy, prostatic hyperplasia, carcinoma penis and prostate; female genital system – carcinoma cervix, carcinoma endometrium, uterine fibroids, vesicular mole and choriocarcinoma, ovarian cyst and tumours; breast – fibrocystic changes, fibroadenoma, carcinoma breast; central nervous system – meningitis, encephalitis, stroke, tumours of CNS

units.title: Pathology II – Clinical Pathology: Body Fluids, Urine and Faeces
units.topics: Examination of body cavity fluids – methods of collection and examination of CSF and other body cavity fluids (sputum, wound discharge) for diagnosis and prognosis; analysis of semen – sperm count, motility and morphology and their importance in infertility; urine – physical characteristics, analysis, culture and sensitivity; faeces – characteristics, stool examination for occult blood, ova, parasites and cysts, reducing substances; methods and collection of urine and faeces for various tests

units.title: Genetics I – Introduction: Nature, Principles and Perspectives of Heredity
units.topics: Application of human genetics in nursing; impact of genetic condition on families; review of cell division – mitosis and meiosis; characteristics and structure of genes; chromosomes – sex determination; chromosomal aberrations; patterns of inheritance – Mendelian theory, multiple allelism and blood groups, sex-linked inheritance; mechanism of inheritance; errors in transmission (mutation)

units.title: Genetics II – Maternal, Prenatal and Genetic Influences on Development of Defects and Diseases
units.topics: Conditions affecting the mother – genetic and infections; consanguinity, atopy; prenatal nutrition and food allergies; maternal age; maternal drug therapy; prenatal testing and diagnosis; effect of radiation, drugs and chemicals; infertility; spontaneous abortion; neural tube defects and the role of folic acid in lowering the risks; Down syndrome (trisomy 21)

units.title: Genetics III – Genetic Testing in the Neonates and Children
units.topics: Screening for congenital abnormalities, developmental delay and dysmorphism; newborn screening for inborn errors and other genetic conditions

units.title: Genetics IV – Genetic Conditions of Adolescents and Adults
units.topics: Cancer genetics – familial cancer; inborn errors of metabolism; blood group alleles and haematological disorders; genetic haemochromatosis; Huntington's disease; mental illness

units.title: Genetics V – Services related to Genetics
units.topics: Genetic testing; gene therapy; genetic counselling; legal and ethical issues; role of the nurse

courses.title: Adult Health Nursing II with integrated pathophysiology including Geriatric Nursing (and Palliative Care module)

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Disorders of Ear, Nose and Throat
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of ear, nose and throat; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; external ear – deformities, otalgia, foreign bodies, tumours; middle ear – impacted wax, tympanic membrane perforation, otitis media, mastoiditis, otosclerosis, tumours; inner ear – Meniere's disease, labyrinthitis, ototoxicity, tumours; upper respiratory airway infections – rhinitis, sinusitis, tonsillitis, laryngitis; epistaxis, nasal obstruction, laryngeal obstruction, cancer of oral cavity and larynx; deafness and its management, hearing aids

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Disorders of Eye
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the eye; history, physical and diagnostic assessment; refractive errors; eyelids – infection and deformities; conjunctiva – inflammation, infection, bleeding; cornea – inflammation and infection; lens – cataract; glaucoma; retinal detachment; blindness; eye donation, eye banking and corneal transplantation

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Kidney and Urinary Problems
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the genitourinary system; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; urinary tract infections – acute, chronic, lower, upper; nephritis, nephrotic syndrome; renal calculi; acute and chronic renal failure (AKI, CKD), dialysis and renal transplantation; disorders of ureter, urinary bladder and urethra; disorders of prostate – inflammation, infection, stricture, obstruction and benign prostatic hypertrophy

units.title: Nursing Management of Disorders of Male Reproductive System
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the male reproductive system; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; infections of testis, penis and adjacent structures – phimosis, epididymitis, orchitis; hydrocele, varicocele, testicular torsion, hypospadias and epispadias; sexual dysfunction, infertility, contraception; male breast disorders – gynaecomastia, tumour, climacteric changes

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Burns, Reconstructive and Cosmetic Surgery
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of skin and connective tissues; history, physical assessment, assessment of burns and fluid and electrolyte loss; burns; reconstructive and cosmetic surgery for burns, congenital deformities, injuries and cosmetic purposes, gender reassignment; legal and ethical aspects; special therapies – vacuum-assisted dressing, laser, liposuction, skin rejuvenation, dermal fillers

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Neurological Disorders
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the nervous system; history, physical and neurological assessment, diagnostic tests; headache; head injuries; spinal injuries – paraplegia, hemiplegia, quadriplegia; spinal cord compression – herniation of intervertebral disc; intracranial and cerebral aneurysms; meningitis, encephalitis, brain abscess, neurocysticercosis; movement disorders – chorea; seizures and epilepsies; cerebrovascular accident; cranial and spinal neuropathies – Bell's palsy, trigeminal neuralgia; peripheral neuropathies; degenerative diseases – Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease; Guillain–Barré syndrome, myasthenia gravis, multiple sclerosis; brain tumours; rehabilitation of patients with neurological deficit

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Immunological Problems
units.topics: Review of the immune system; nursing assessment – history and physical assessment; HIV and AIDS – epidemiology, transmission, prevention of transmission and management; opportunistic infections; role of the nurse – counselling, health education, home care and rehabilitation; National AIDS Control Programme (NACO) and other national and international agencies

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Oncological Conditions (including Palliative Care Module)
units.topics: Structure and characteristics of normal and cancer cells; history, physical assessment, diagnostic tests; prevention, screening, early detection, warning signs of cancer; epidemiology, aetiology, classification, pathophysiology, staging, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment modalities and nursing management; common malignancies – eye, ear, nose, larynx, breast, cervix, ovary, uterus, sarcoma, kidney, bladder, prostate, brain, spinal cord; oncological emergencies; modalities of treatment – chemotherapy, radiotherapy (radiation safety, AERB regulations), surgery, stem cell and bone marrow transplant, immunotherapy, gene therapy; psychological aspects of cancer; supportive care; hospice care; palliative care – principles, symptom management, pain, end-of-life care, alternative therapies

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients in Emergency and Disaster Situations
units.topics: Disaster nursing – concept, principles and related policies; types of disaster – natural and man-made; disaster preparedness – team, guidelines, protocols, equipment, resources; triage; medical and surgical emergencies – polytrauma, bites and stings, poisoning, thermal emergencies (heat stroke, hypothermia, frostbite), drowning; principles of emergency management; emergency drugs; medicolegal aspects

units.title: Nursing Care of the Elderly
units.topics: Nursing assessment – history and physical assessment; ageing – demography, myths and realities, theories of ageing; age-related body system changes; cognitive and psychosocial aspects of ageing; medications and the elderly; stress and coping in older adults; common health problems and nursing management; psychosocial and sexual abuse of the elderly; role of nurse in care of elderly and their caregivers; use of aids and prostheses (hearing aids, dentures); legal and ethical issues; provisions, programmes and privileges for the elderly; home and institutional care

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients in Critical Care Units
units.topics: Principles of critical care nursing; organisation – physical set-up, policies, staffing norms; protocols, equipment and supplies; critical care biomedical equipment – ventilators, cardiac monitors, defibrillators, infusion pumps, resuscitation equipment; mechanical ventilation and its complications; advanced cardiac life support; nursing management of the critically ill patient; transitional care; ethical and legal aspects; breaking bad news – communication with patient and family; end-of-life care

units.title: Nursing Management of Adults including Elderly with Occupational and Industrial Disorders
units.topics: History, physical examination, diagnostic tests; occupational diseases – pneumoconioses (silicosis, asbestosis, coal workers' lung, byssosis), occupational dermatoses, noise-induced hearing loss, lead and other poisoning, occupational cancers; prevention, control and management; occupational health services and legislation

courses.title: Professionalism, Professional Values and Ethics including Bioethics

units.title: Professionalism
units.topics: Profession – definition, characteristics; nursing as a profession; professionalism – definition and characteristics, attributes (accountability, competence, commitment, integrity, collaboration), challenges of professionalism; personal identity versus professional identity; preservation of self-integrity; professional conduct – following rules, policies, code of conduct, dress code; professional etiquette and behaviours; professional boundaries; social media use; professional socialisation; role of nurse in maintaining professionalism

units.title: Professional Values
units.topics: Values – definition, characteristics, types; value clarification and value formation; personal and professional values; core professional values – human dignity, integrity, altruism, autonomy, social justice, caring, confidentiality, accountability; ICN and INC codes; professional values in transcultural care; advocacy – patient advocacy; developing and strengthening professional values

units.title: Ethics and Bioethics
units.topics: Ethics and morality – definitions, ethical theories; ethical principles – autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, veracity, fidelity, confidentiality; bioethics – definition, scope; ethical issues and dilemmas in nursing; ethical decision-making models; code of ethics and code of professional conduct (INC, ICN); patient rights and responsibilities, Charter of Patient Rights; ethics committees; beginning-of-life issues (MTP, ART, surrogacy, prenatal sex determination); end-of-life issues (euthanasia, advance directives, DNR, withdrawal of life support); organ donation and transplantation; research ethics and informed consent; ethics in psychiatric, paediatric and geriatric care; whistle-blowing; allocation of scarce resources

courses.title: Child Health Nursing I (including ENBC, FBNC, IMNCI and PLS modules)

units.title: Introduction: Modern Concepts of Child-care
units.topics: Historical development of child health; philosophy and modern concept of child-care; cultural and religious considerations; national policy, legislations, programmes and agencies for child health and welfare; internationally accepted rights of the child; changing trends in hospital care – preventive, promotive and curative; preventive paediatrics – concept, immunization, UIP and cold chain, under-five and well-baby clinics, prevention of accidents; child morbidity and mortality rates; differences between adult and child in response to illness; hospital environment, impact of hospitalization on child and family, communication with children, grief and bereavement; role of the child health nurse; principles of pre- and post-operative care of infants and children; paediatric procedures – administration of medication (oral, IM, IV), calculation of fluid requirement, application of restraints, pain assessment (FACES, FLACC, numerical scales)

units.title: The Healthy Child
units.topics: Definition and principles of growth and development; factors affecting growth and development; growth and development from birth to adolescence; theories of growth and development (Freud, Erikson, Piaget, Kohlberg); needs of normal children through the stages of development and parental guidance; nutritional needs of infants and children – breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding, supplementary/artificial feeding and weaning; Baby Friendly Hospital concept; types and value of play and selection of play material

units.title: Nursing Care of Neonate
units.topics: Appraisal of the newborn; nursing care of the normal newborn – essential newborn care; neonatal resuscitation; nursing management of the low birth weight baby; kangaroo mother care; nursing management of common neonatal disorders – hyperbilirubinemia, hypothermia, hyperthermia, metabolic disorders, neonatal infections, neonatal seizures, respiratory distress syndrome, retinopathy of prematurity; organization of the neonatal care unit; neonatal equipment (ENBC and FBNC modules)

units.title: Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illnesses (IMNCI)
units.topics: Concept, principles and components of IMNCI; assess, classify, identify treatment, treat, counsel and follow up the sick young infant (up to 2 months) and the sick child (2 months to 5 years); IMNCI case management process and chart booklet (IMNCI module)

units.title: Nursing Management in Common Childhood Diseases
units.topics: Respiratory system – congenital malformations (tracheo-oesophageal fistula, diaphragmatic hernia); acute nasopharyngitis, tonsillitis, croup, bronchitis, bronchiolitis, pneumonia, asthma; endocrine system – juvenile diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism

units.title: Childhood Emergencies
units.topics: Accidents – causes and prevention; poisoning; foreign bodies; haemorrhage; burns and drowning; Paediatric Life Support (PLS) as per AHA guidelines (PLS module)

courses.title: Mental Health Nursing I

units.title: Introduction
units.topics: Perspectives of mental health and mental health nursing; evolution of mental health services, treatments and nursing practices; mental health team; nature and scope of mental health nursing; role and functions of the mental health nurse in various settings; factors affecting the level of nursing practice; concepts of normal and abnormal behaviour

units.title: Principles and Concepts of Mental Health Nursing
units.topics: Definitions and terminology; classification of mental disorders – ICD-11, DSM-5, geropsychiatry manual classification; review of personality development and defence mechanisms; aetiology – bio-psycho-social factors; psychopathology of mental disorders – review of structure and function of the brain, limbic system and neurotransmission; principles of mental health nursing; ethics and responsibilities; practice standards for psychiatric mental health nursing (INC practice standards); conceptual models – existential, psychoanalytical, behavioural, interpersonal; preventive psychiatry and rehabilitation

units.title: Mental Health Assessment
units.topics: History taking; mental status examination; mini mental status examination; neurological examination; investigations – related blood chemistry, EEG, CT and MRI; psychological tests

units.title: Therapeutic Communication and Nurse-Patient Relationship
units.topics: Therapeutic communication – types, techniques, characteristics and barriers; therapeutic nurse-patient relationship – phases, interpersonal relationship; elements of the nurse-patient contract; review of the Johari window; therapeutic impasse and its management

units.title: Treatment Modalities and Therapies Used in Mental Disorders
units.topics: Physical therapies – psychopharmacology, electroconvulsive therapy; psychological therapies – psychotherapy, behaviour therapy, cognitive behaviour therapy; psychosocial – group therapy, family therapy, therapeutic community, recreational therapy, art therapy (dance, music), occupational therapy; alternative and complementary – yoga, meditation, relaxation; considerations for special populations

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Schizophrenia and Other Psychotic Disorders
units.topics: Prevalence and incidence; classification; aetiology, psychodynamics, clinical manifestations and diagnostic criteria; nursing process – history, physical and mental assessment; treatment modalities and nursing management; geriatric considerations and considerations for special populations; follow-up, home care and rehabilitation

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Mood Disorders
units.topics: Prevalence and incidence; mood disorders – bipolar affective disorder, mania, depression and dysthymia; aetiology, psychodynamics, clinical manifestations and diagnosis; nursing assessment – history, physical and mental assessment; treatment modalities and nursing management; geriatric considerations and special populations; follow-up, home care and rehabilitation

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatisation Disorders
units.topics: Prevalence and incidence; classification; anxiety disorders – OCD, PTSD, somatoform disorders, phobias, dissociative and conversion disorders; aetiology, psychodynamics, clinical manifestations and diagnostic criteria; nursing assessment; treatment modalities and nursing management; geriatric considerations and special populations; follow-up, home care and rehabilitation

courses.title: Community Health Nursing I including Environmental Science & Epidemiology

units.title: Concepts of Community Health and Community Health Nursing
units.topics: Definitions – public health, community health and community health nursing; public health in India and its evolution; scope of community health nursing; concepts of health and illness/disease – dimensions and determinants of health; natural history of disease; levels of prevention – primary, secondary and tertiary; health problems (profile) of India

units.title: Health Care Planning and Organization of Health Care at Various Levels
units.topics: Health planning steps; health planning in India – committees and commissions on health and family welfare, Five Year Plans; participation of community and stakeholders; health care delivery system in India – infrastructure and health sectors, delivery of health services at sub-centre, PHC, CHC, district, state and national levels; Sustainable Development Goals; primary health care and comprehensive primary health care – elements, principles, delivery through SC/Health and Wellness Centres (Ayushman Arogya Mandir), role of MLHP/CHO; national health policies 1983, 2002, 2017; National Health Mission (NRHM, NUHM), Ayushman Bharat and universal health coverage

units.title: Environmental Science, Environmental Health and Sanitation
units.topics: Natural resources – renewable and non-renewable, associated problems, role of an individual in conservation; ecosystems – concept, structure, function, types, energy flow; biodiversity – classification, value, threats and conservation; environmental pollution – air, water, soil, marine, noise, thermal and nuclear – causes, effects and control; climate change, global warming, acid rain, ozone layer depletion, wasteland reclamation; social issues and the environment – sustainable development, urban problems, environmental ethics, environmental protection Acts; environmental health and sanitation – safe water, water-borne diseases, purification of water, drinking water standards, water quality testing; rainwater harvesting and watershed management; role of the nurse in pollution prevention; disposal of solid waste, human excreta and sewage; insecticides and pesticides

units.title: Nutrition Assessment and Nutrition Education
units.topics: Review of nutrition, meal planning and diet plans for different age groups; nutrition assessment of individuals, families and community; planning diets based on locally available food, dietary habits and economic status; nutrition education, counselling and rehabilitation; nutritional deficiency disorders; national nutrition policy and programmes; food-borne diseases – burden, causes, transmission, early identification, initial management and referral; food poisoning and food intoxication – types, features, prevention, control and public health response

units.title: Communication Management and Health Education
units.topics: Behaviour change communication (BCC) – skills, communication in human behaviour; health belief model; ways to influence behaviour, steps and techniques of behaviour change, guiding principles and steps in planning BCC; social and behaviour change communication (SBCC) strategies; collecting social history; barriers to communication and ways to overcome them; health promotion and health education – methods and audio-visual aids

units.title: Community Health Nursing Approaches, Concepts, Roles and Responsibilities of Community Health Nursing Personnel
units.topics: Approaches – nursing process, epidemiological, problem-solving, evidence-based and empowerment approaches; review of primary health care and comprehensive primary health care; home visit – concept, principles, process and techniques, bag technique; qualities of a community health nurse; roles and responsibilities of community health nursing personnel in family health services; review of principles and techniques of counselling

units.title: Assisting Individuals and Families to Promote and Maintain their Health
units.topics: Assessment of individuals – children, women, adolescents and elderly; growth and development, milestones, anthropometry, BMI; monitoring of temperature and BP, menstrual cycle, breast self-examination and testicular self-examination, warning signs of diseases; basic tests – urine sugar and albumin, blood sugar, haemoglobin; primary care – routine check-ups, immunization, counselling, diagnosis and management of common conditions, standing orders, drug dispensing, therapeutic procedures, follow-up care; maintenance of client and facility records, report writing; social issues – women empowerment, abuse of women, children and elders, female foeticide, commercial sex workers, substance abuse; community resources – trauma services, old age homes, orphanages, homes for the disabled and destitute, palliative and hospice care, assisted living

units.title: Introduction to Epidemiology – Epidemiological Approaches and Processes
units.topics: Concept and definition of epidemiology; distribution and frequency of disease; aims and uses of epidemiology; epidemiological models of causation of disease; concepts of disease transmission – direct, indirect, chain of infection; time trends in disease occurrence; epidemiological approaches – descriptive, analytical, experimental; principles of control measures and levels of prevention; investigation of an epidemic of communicable disease; use of basic epidemiological tools for community diagnosis

units.title: Communicable Diseases and National Health Programmes
units.topics: Vector-borne diseases – malaria, filaria, kala-azar, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya; epidemiology, prevention, control, screening, diagnosis, primary management, referral and follow-up of leprosy, tuberculosis, vaccine-preventable diseases, enteric fever, viral hepatitis, HIV/AIDS and STI/RTI, diarrhoea, respiratory tract infections, COVID-19, helminthic infections, scabies and pediculosis, zoonotic diseases including rabies; role of the nurse in control of communicable diseases; national programmes – UIP, NLEP, NTEP, IDSP, NACP, NVBDCP, national air quality monitoring and newly added programmes

units.title: Non-communicable Diseases and National Health Programmes
units.topics: National response to NCDs; epidemiology, prevention, screening, primary management, referral and follow-up of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, stroke and obesity; blindness – categories of visual impairment and the national programme for control of blindness; deafness – national programme for prevention and control of deafness; thyroid diseases; injuries and accidents – risk factors of road traffic injuries, operational guidelines for trauma care on highways; cancers – cervix, breast and oral: risk factors, prevention, screening, early management and referral; palliative care; role of the nurse in NCD control; NPCDCS/NP-NCD, national cancer control programme, National Tobacco Control Programme, standard treatment protocols

units.title: School Health Services
units.topics: Objectives of school health services; health problems of school children; components of school health services; maintenance of school health records; initiation and planning of school health services; role of the school health nurse

units.title: Introduction and Theoretical Foundations
units.topics: Education and educational technology – definition, aims, approaches and scope; latest approaches to education – transformational, relationship-based and competency-based education; educational philosophy – definition, philosophies of education, philosophy of nursing education; teaching-learning process – definitions, nature, characteristics, principles and barriers; learning theories; latest approaches – experiential, reflective, scenario-based, simulation-based and blended learning

units.title: Assessment and Planning
units.topics: Assessment of the teacher – essential qualities, teaching styles (formal authority, demonstrator, facilitator, delegator); assessment of learners – types of learners, determinants of learning (learning needs, readiness, learning styles), today's generation of learners, emotional intelligence, motivational factors; curriculum planning – definition, types, curriculum design components and approaches, curriculum development – factors, facilitators and barriers; writing learning outcomes/behavioural objectives; course plan, unit plan and lesson plan

units.title: Implementation
units.topics: Principles and strategies of classroom management; effective classroom communication – facilitators and barriers; information and communication technology (ICT) in education; teaching methods – lecture, discussion, microteaching, skill lab, symposium, panel discussion, seminar, workshop, exhibition, role play, project, field trip, self-directed learning, computer-assisted learning, one-to-one instruction; active learning strategies – team-based learning, problem-based learning, peer sharing, case study analysis, journaling, debate, gaming, interprofessional education

units.title: Teaching in the Clinical Setting
units.topics: Clinical learning environment; factors influencing selection of clinical learning experiences; practice models; characteristics of an effective clinical teacher; writing clinical learning outcomes; clinical teaching strategies – patient assignment, clinical conference, bedside clinic, case study/care study, nursing rounds, concept mapping, project, debate, game, role play, PBL, questioning, written assignment, process recording

units.title: Educational/Teaching Media
units.topics: Media use – purpose, components, principles and steps; types of media – still visuals (non-projected: drawings, diagrams, charts, graphs, posters, cartoons, board devices; projected: overhead and slide projectors, LCD/multimedia presentations), moving visuals (video, films), realia and models, audio aids, electronic media/computer learning resources, computer simulations, virtual reality, telecommunication and distance education, mobile technology

units.title: Assessment/Evaluation Methods/Strategies
units.topics: Purposes, scope and principles in selection of assessment methods; barriers to evaluation; guidelines to develop assessment tests; assessment of knowledge – essay, short answer, multiple choice questions (single and multiple response); assessment of skills – clinical evaluation, observation (checklist, rating scales, videotapes), written communication, verbal communication (oral examination), simulation, OSCE, self-evaluation, clinical portfolio and logbooks; assessment of attitude – attitude scales; assessment tests for higher learning – interpretive questions, hot spot, drag and drop, ordered response

units.title: Guidance/Academic Advising, Counselling and Discipline
units.topics: Guidance – definition, objectives, scope, purpose, principles, roles of faculty; counselling – difference from guidance, definition, objectives, scope, principles, types, process, steps, skills and techniques, roles of the counsellor, organization of counselling services; counselling issues and needs of nursing students; discipline and grievance in students – managing disciplinary and grievance problems, preventive guidance and counselling, role of the grievance redressal cell

units.title: Ethics and Evidence-based Teaching in Nursing Education
units.topics: Ethics – review; ethical considerations in nursing education; value-based education; ethical decision-making and ethical standards for students; student-faculty relationship; evidence-based teaching – introduction and application in nursing education

courses.title: Introduction to Forensic Nursing and Indian Laws
courses.paper: Introduction to Forensic Nursing and Indian Laws

units.title: Forensic Science and Violence
units.topics: Forensic science – definition, history, importance in medical science, forensic science laboratory; violence – definition, epidemiology, sources of data; sexual abuse of children and women

units.title: Forensic Nursing
units.topics: Definition; history and development; scope – practice settings, areas of practice and subspecialties; ethical issues; roles and responsibilities of the nurse; INC and State Nursing Council Acts

units.title: Forensic Team and Role of the Forensic Nurse
units.topics: Members of the forensic team and their roles; comprehensive forensic nursing care of the victim and family – physical, psychosocial, cultural and spiritual, legal aspects; assisting the forensic team in care beyond the nurse's scope; admission, discharge, referral and death of the victim; nurse as a witness; evidence preservation – observation, recognition, collection, preservation, documentation of biological and other evidence, forwarding of biological samples for forensic examination

units.title: Introduction of Indian Constitution and Human Rights
units.topics: Introduction to the Indian Constitution; fundamental rights – rights of victims and rights of accused persons; Human Rights Commission

units.title: Sources of Laws, Indian Judicial System and Indian Laws
units.topics: Sources of laws and law-making powers; overview of the Indian judicial system – Judicial Magistrate First Class, district, state and apex courts; civil and criminal case procedures; overview of the criminal laws (Indian Penal Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, Indian Evidence Act – now Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023); overview of the POCSO Act and its importance

units.title: Cardiovascular, Haematological, Gastrointestinal, Genitourinary and Nervous System Disorders
topics: Congenital heart diseases – cyanotic and acyanotic (ASD, VSD, PDA, tetralogy of Fallot)
Rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease; congestive cardiac failure
Haematological conditions – haemophilia, thalassaemia, anaemia, leukaemia, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma
